meaning: something that is very easy to do
example: The math test was a piece of cake.
origin: The exact origin is uncertain. It is an informal expression from American English in the early 1900s.

wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the literal meaning of the words, not the idiomatic one.
The idiom means the opposite: something that is very easy.
The idiom has nothing to do with gifts or friends.

explanation: 'A piece of cake' is an informal way to say that something is very easy to do. It is not about food.
